notes: Italy: Mediaset holds exclusive domestic rights for 2024-25 to 2026-27 (2026-27 is the last season of the cycle). Every match is free-to-air on Mediaset channels: the 2026-27 round of 64 (14-17 Aug 2026) aired on Italia 1 and 20, streamed on Mediaset Infinity and sportmediaset.it. Internationally, Lega Serie A sells the Coppa Italia with the Supercoppa as a cups package, usually to different partners than Serie A. No 2026-27 country list has been published. International entries therefore use the latest official Lega Serie A list: the broadcasters for the 2024-25 final (Milan v Bologna, 50+ broadcasters, about 180 countries), cross-checked against the near-identical official list for the 2025-26 Supercoppa (Dec 2025, 53 broadcasters, 180+ territories) and Wikipedia's 2024-2027 Coppa Italia table. Where Wikipedia differs, the note says so. The only confirmed 2026-27 international deals are in the US: CBS/Paramount+ (English, at least 20 Coppa Italia matches) and Telemundo (Spanish, 2026-27 to 2028-29). Infront manages Serie A, Coppa Italia and Supercoppa rights in 36 APAC territories for 2024-25 to 2026-27. Per Wikipedia, in countries with no rights holder matches are on the official Serie A YouTube channel.

broadcasters.note: Mediaset holds exclusive rights 2024-25 to 2026-27, with all matches free (in chiaro). The round of 64 (14-17 Aug 2026) was split between Italia 1 and 20, with live streaming on Mediaset Infinity and sportmediaset.it. Channel allocation for later rounds and the final was not published in the sources read; other Mediaset channels such as Canale 5 may be used. The official Lega Serie A Coppa Italia broadcasters page lists Mediaset (Mediaset Infinity) for Italy.

2026-27 confirmed. English: CBS Sports' one-year extension for 2026-27 includes at least 20 Coppa Italia matches, mainly on Paramount+ (SBJ via MarketScale; renderfoot). Spanish: Telemundo holds Coppa Italia rights 2026-27 to 2028-29 across Telemundo, Universo, Peacock and the FAST channel Telemundo Deportes Ahora. How matches are split between platforms is not published, so only some may air on free broadcast TV. CBS's rights also cover various Caribbean and Pacific territories (Lega Serie A list).
